caption: Warm chocolate sauce is poured over a scoop of ice cream, and the sauce firms into a crackly shell on the cold surface.

sa.check: Chocolate sauce is poured over the scoop.
The sauce flows down the scoop.
The sauce firms into a shell on the ice cream.
The set shell looks dull rather than glossy.
The order is pour, flow, set.

pc.expect: The sauce's change runs one way where it lies on the cold scoop: it slows, stops and stays set.
pc.fail: A set patch of shell turns runny again and flows on with no fresh sauce over it; or the shell draws back up the scoop; or the shell alternates between glossy and runny and dull and set.

pc.expect: The sauce arrives as a thin liquid that flows and coats, and where it sets it is a rigid shell that cracks rather than flows.
pc.fail: The set shell sags or drips as the scoop is moved; or the sauce sets as a soft skin that stretches; or the shell crumbles to dust; or the sauce stands as a rigid ridge before it has stopped flowing.

pc.expect: The sauce runs downward over the scoop's sides and any excess falls to the dish.
pc.fail: The sauce climbs the scoop; or a run travels up over the scoop's top; or a drip leaves the scoop and floats; or sauce gathers under the scoop and rises around it.

pc.expect: The ice cream shows the sauce arriving: the surface it covers goes dark, and the scoop goes wet and glossy where the warm sauce lies.
pc.fail: Sauce runs over the scoop and the surface under it stays pale and untouched; or the shell forms on a part of the scoop no sauce reached; or the scoop stays sharp-edged and dry where sauce has pooled on it.

pc.expect: One scoop and one stream of sauce; the sauce goes from the jug to the scoop to the dish and nowhere else.
pc.fail: Sauce appears on the dish with none running off the scoop; or the scoop grows; or a second scoop appears; or the sauce passes through the scoop and out below it.

pc.expect: The bare ice cream's colour, the dish and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: The bare ice cream changes colour; or the dish changes pattern; or items on the table rearrange.
